summary: A 'world forest' planting trees and herbs from the continents around symbolic global themes, one of the campus's quieter green tickets.
description:
Vishwa Van assembles a diplomatic garden: trees, shrubs and medicinal plants representing the world's regions, planted in themed sections meant to make a unity-of-nations point beside the statue that makes a unity-of-India one. Botanically it is a young collection still growing into its concept; as a visit it is a quiet, uncrowded walk with interpretation boards and shade.

Pick it if you are on a two-day campus plan, enjoy plants, or want the least-queued ticket on the circuit; first-day visitors with limited hours should spend them on the bigger draws.
highlights: Quietest garden ticket on the campus

modes.road: On the campus circuit; e-buses stop nearby

seasonality.notes: Cool months for walking; monsoon keeps it green.

experience.photography_notes: Themed sections give tidy frames; nothing here demands more than soft morning light.

emergency.nearest_hospital: Ekta Nagar facilities; Rajpipla civil hospital (~25 km)

tips: Second-day ticket, don't spend first-day hours here

seo.meta_description: The world-forest garden at the SoU campus: what it is, tickets and when it earns a slot.
